“We expect the beat to be primarily driven by revenue momentum in optical-enterprise and a rebound in optical-carrier sequential growth, offsetting weakness in glass innovations where smartphone is partly balanced by stable display performance,” analysts led by Joseph Cardoso said.

Although the brokerage forecast strong earnings print for the firm, it sees the setup as less compelling against buy-side expectations, which “will likely need a more material catalyst, such as a raise to the internal Springboard 2028 revenue target and operating margin target of 'at or above 20%,'” it said.

JPMorgan lowered its price target on the stock to $165 from $170, valuing Corning at 27 times its 2028 earnings estimate, down from 30 times previously, in line with lower valuations across optical industry peers.
Analysts at Seeking Alpha had a contrasting view on the optical fiber manufacturer.
downgraded Corning to Sell from Hold due to high valuation, aggressive growth assumptions, and a relatively weaker technological edge in the AI photonics trade.

“The main risk for Corning is the same for most AI data center suppliers: a delay or cancellation of data center builds that may leave it with overcapacity, weaker growth, and margins. Near-term operating risks are cost increases, particularly helium that is used in high-density fiber optic manufacturing, as well as energy costs,” Fernandez said.

Over the last 3 months, EPS estimates have seen 9 upward revisions and 2 downward moves while revenue estimates have seen 6 upward revisions and 2 downward moves—representing an overall optimistic stance among analysts. Over the last 2 years, GLW has beaten EPS and revenue estimates 100% of the time, further fueling optimism.

title: Corning Q3 preview: AI demand drives revenue optimism, but investors may need bigger catalyst
